items.title: TTL Cache
items.text: An LRU cache decorator with a time to live. ttl_lru_cache works exactly like functools.lru_cache, except entries automatically expire after a configurable number of seconds.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
pipuv 
pip install ttl-cache-decorator

uv add ttl-cache-decorator

Requires Python 3.12+.

items.title: Quickstart
How it works
items.text:
Under the hood it still uses lru_cache, but the cached call receives an extra positional-only time bucket argument derived from a monotonic clock:

The time bucket
time_bucket = int((time.monotonic() + offset) // ttl)

An entry stays "alive" while the bucket value is unchanged and expires when the bucket rolls over:

graph LR
  A[Call] --> B{Bucket changed?}
  B -->|No| C[Serve cached value]
  B -->|Yes| D[Recompute and cache]
  C --> E[Return]
  D --> E

Note

The bucket boundary is shared per TTL window, so an entry lives for at most ttl seconds and at least the remainder of the current bucket.

items.title: ttl_lru_cache
items.text:
ttl_lru_cache(
    ttl: float = 60,
    jitter: float = 0,
    maxsize: int | None = 128,
    typed: bool = False,
)
Parameter Type Default Description ttl float 60 Time to live in seconds. Must be positive. jitter float 0 Max random offset (seconds) applied to bucket boundaries. Must be non-negative. maxsize int \| None 128 Max size of the cache, or None for unbounded. typed bool False Whether argument types are part of the cache key.

Returns a decorator whose wrapped function keeps its signature and exposes the usual lru_cache helpers: cache_info() and cache_clear().

Validation

A ValueError is raised at decoration time if ttl is not positive or jitter is negative.

items.title: Jitter
items.text:
jitter draws a random offset once per decorated function from random.uniform(0, jitter), so different functions (or processes) expire at different moments instead of all at once. Use it to avoid a thundering herd when many cached values would otherwise expire simultaneously:

Adding jitter
@ttl_lru_cache(ttl=60, jitter=10)
def fetch_metrics(service: str) -> dict:
    ...

items.title: Cache helpers
items.text:
Inspecting and clearing the cache
fetch_user.cache_info()   # CacheInfo(hits=..., misses=..., maxsize=128, currsize=...)
fetch_user.cache_clear()  # Drop all cached entries
Typing

The decorator is fully generic via ParamSpec and returns a TTLCachedFunction protocol, so type checkers preserve the wrapped function's signature — including keyword arguments.

from ttl_cache import TTLCachedFunction

cached_fetch: TTLCachedFunction[[str], dict] = ttl_lru_cache(ttl=5)(fetch_user)
